Keep in mind that this project is a self-teaching project for learning the elements of computing systems. The code is intentionally written in a simple and straightforward manner to facilitate understanding. Avoid using advanced or complex programming constructs that may hinder the learning process.

Preserve existing documentation and comments. Do not delete or rewrite them when implementing code. If a documentation change seems necessary, e.g., a typo or an error, keep it minimal and explain why; ask before making substantial changes.

When writing code, avoid opaque bit-manipulation shortcuts such as shifts and masks when clearer iterator-based or arithmetic operations are available. Bitwise operations are appropriate when they directly model a logic gate or chip behavior.

Do not run command-line validation commands, such as tests, builds, or formatting checks, unless I explicitly ask. Instead, tell me which command(s) to run and wait for me to share the results.
